correctness.rationale: Complete exact finite face-poset construction via independent k-set enumeration and all subfaces, for each of five parameters. Sequential toggling by all \(3k+3\) vertices yields a valid acyclic matching by the cited general element-matching theorem. The code checks faces=\(2\cdot\mathrm{pairs}+1\), the only survivor mask 21846 has eight vertices, and the empty face was matched. Forman discrete Morse implies \(S^7\). Independent Python enumeration reproduced \(k\in\{4,5,6\}\). No claim beyond five finite k values.

originality.rationale: Primary source comparison shows a published conjecture for these same five total-cut homotopy types, with proofs only for \(k=3\) and \(n=3k+1,3k+2\). At \((k,n)=(4,15)\) the older table gives \(H_7\cong\mathbb Z\), not the homotopy equivalence. Exhaustive finite certificates establish stronger homotopy results across the five cases, including \((k,n)=(7,24)\) and \((k,n)=(8,27)\) beyond published computational support. Semantic index searches found no stronger/equivalent proof; unindexed overlap remains a risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent unindexed mathematical work may exist; scientific novelty cannot be proven by unsuccessful index searches.

value.rationale: The cases lie exactly on the \(i=3\) diagonal of Bayer et al. Conjecture 5.1, which is unresolved in Shen et al. beyond the \(i=1,2\) proof. They prove complete homotopy types, not just previously known \(k=4\) Betti numbers; the two larger parameter pairs go beyond Bayer et al. reported Sage parameter range. Five consecutive natural cases make a useful finite cutoff; the claim is not an arbitrary slice or fabricated all-parameter theorem.
